item.title: UTSA vs. Tulsa: 5 players to watch as Roadrunners look to secure home field for American championship
item.description: UTSA Roadrunners quarterback Owen McCown runs the ball in a game against South Florida at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas on Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) After UTSA survived with a 19-17 win last week against UAB , coach Jeff Traylor's first instinct was to shield quarterback Owen McCown from the cameras and microphones. McCown hit just 12 of 20 passes for 112 yards with an interception in the win, marking a second straight quiet week after he threw for 85 yards with no touchdowns and an interception in the previous game against North Texas. The combined total of 197 passing yards is the lowest in any two-game stretch across McCown's three years as the Roadrunners starter. Though he acknowledged McCown "wasn't as sharp as he's been," Traylor also understood that quarterbacks shoulder an outsized portion of the credit or blame for the offensive performance, with many observers overlooking the protection issues or struggles at receiver that sometimes make McCown's life more challenging. But despite Traylor's instinct to allow McCown a moment out of the spotlight, McCown volunteered for a trip to the postgame interview room, facing the media before he'd even had time to change out of his cleats. "He's a man of ownership," Traylor said. "He's a tough, tough young man. For him to stand in front of the media and say that, I wasn't even going to let y'all have him, but he wanted to own it. That's just who that dude is, man. He's a stud." READ MORE: What UTSA's Jeff Traylor said about the coaching vacancy at TCU McCown called the opening half against the Blazers "my worst half of football I've ever played," marred by an interception deep in Roadrunners' territory that allowed UAB to punch in a tying touchdown just before halftime. But after watching UTSA's defense carry the team to a victory, McCown said he felt encouraged about the prospect of learning and building from those mistakes. "It was really just me hurting myself," McCown said. "It was uncharacteristic to me. I won't ever play a half like that again. It was rare for me. I had a couple of missed throws. I thought the reads were right, just wasn't going my way, and that'll happen. It's a full team game, though. And we came out with the win, so it's a lot easier to learn from." item.title: One year after Ji'Ayir Brown's curious claim of elite status, 49ers safety sounds prophetic
item.description: San Francisco 49ers safety Ji'Ayir Brown celebrates after a play against the Minnesota Vikings in the second half Sunday in Mexico City. (Gregory Payan/Associated Press) Last year, when Ji'Ayir Brown was one of the San Francisco 49ers ' backup safeties, he declared he was a top-five player at the position in the NFL. That prompted a logical - if slightly uncomfortable - follow-up question: How could he be among the league's best at his position if his own coaches didn't think he was one of the top two safeties on the roster? Brown didn't hesitate: "It's going to make sense one day." At the time, Brown sounded delusional. At the moment, he's looking prescient. After being benched in each of the previous two seasons, the 2023 third-round pick is enjoying a career-best year in which he ranks ninth among NFL safeties who have played at least 300 snaps, according to Pro Football Focus' grading system. Brown was already undramatically silencing social-media critics he'd acquired during his early career inconsistencies before he made a loud statement in the Niners' 35-10 win over the Vikings on Sunday in Mexico City. With the 49ers leading 21-10 just before halftime, Brown had an 18-yard interception return for a touchdown that signaled the rout was on. Asked about the pick-six, head coach Kyle Shanahan began by referencing Brown's up-and-down career. "Tig's been here for a while with us," Shanahan said, referring to Brown by his nickname. "He's been through a lot with us." The 49ers selected Brown No. 87 overall in 2023 when he was the draft's only player who had at least 10 interceptions over his final two college seasons. The Penn State standout then became a productive fill-in starter as a rookie and intercepted a Patrick Mahomes' pass in the 49ers' overtime loss to the Chiefs in Super Bowl LVIII. However, Brown had just five picks in his first 58 games before Sunday. Last year, he termed himself a "ball hawk," but acknowledged the big plays had been slow to come in the NFL. Last Sunday, however, Brown made a massive play because he was quick to diagnose QB Kirk Cousins' intentions. Lined up near the right hashmark, Brown took two steps to his left, toward the middle of the field, before Cousins took the shotgun snap. At the snap, Brown began running in the same direction while reading Cousins' eyes, which were locked onto wide receiver Tai Felton. Brown stepped in front of Felton, secured the pick and began an untouched jog into the end zone. Brown noted the 49ers faced Cousins in a 38-17 win over the Raiders on Nov. 8, two days before Cousins was traded to Minnesota. "I watched his tape a lot and picked up his mannerisms," Brown said. "I was in the right call to be in the right position." item.title: Why Texas A&M snub worked out for UTSA's Jeff Traylor
item.description: UTSA Roadrunners head coach Jeff Traylor looks on during the first quarter against the Rice Owls in Houston, Texas, Saturday, Oct., 3, 2026. (Zach Del Bello/San Antonio Express-News) Texas A&M did Jeff Traylor a favor. Three years ago, the Aggies interviewed him for an office that eventually makes every occupant miserable, then offered it to Mike Elko instead. Sure, the money would have been nice. But as you watch the men on the sidelines in College Station and San Antonio this Friday, ask yourself: Would you rather have Elko's options right now, or Traylor's? In some ways, they're still in completely different college football worlds. The same day that close to 110,000 people will file into Kyle Field to watch Elko's Aggies try to knock off No. 5 Texas, UTSA will be ecstatic to draw a crowd a third of that size to its regular-season finale at the Alamodome. But that disparity in attention comes with a disparity in expectations, and one of A&M's biggest problems is that it's never figured out the right ratio of the latter to the former. It's been almost three decades since the Aggies last won a conference championship, and 16 years since they've even played for one, and still every time they fall short of contention, it's a crisis. Setting high standards for your coaches is great. But once a fifth or sixth accomplished coach in a row fails to meet them, it might be fair to wonder if there's a difference between what your donor base calls standards and what outsiders call pipe dreams. It's not that coaches can't win at A&M. Kevin Sumlin and Jimbo Fisher managed one Top 5 finish apiece during their six-year tenures, and Elko came close last season. With the Aggies' money, resources and recruiting base, their competitive ceiling remains undeniably high. Their competitive floor, though, is lower than they ever like to acknowledge, and that was true even before a move to the Southeastern Conference made that more obvious. R.C. Slocum, Dennis Franchione and Mike Sherman each endured at least one losing Big 12 season after the Aggies won that league in 1998. UTSA Roadrunners head coach Jeff Traylor after the game against the Rice Owls in Houston, Texas, Saturday, Oct., 3, 2026. (Zach Del Bello/San Antonio Express-News) In the SEC, though, everybody has money, resources and a recruiting base, which reduces the margin for error and increases the likelihood of a crash like A&M's in 2026. Less than 12 months after taking the Aggies to the College Football Playoff, Elko is in danger of becoming the first coach in program history to lose eight conference games in one season. This isn't to say Traylor would have been doomed to the same predicament had the Aggies hired him after his 90-minute Zoom interview in 2023 . item.title: ‘Everything we need’ – Arteta encouraged by Gyokeres’ performance against Dortmund
item.description: ‘Everything we need’ – Arteta encouraged by Gyokeres’ performance against Dortmund Mikel Arteta says Viktor Gyokeres’ performance against Borussia Dortmund provides plenty of encouragement after the striker scored his side’s only goal. Gyokeres produced a superb finish to open the scoring after being awarded a start, having struggled to break into Arteta’s starting 11 so far this season. And the Arsenal boss was equally impressed by the striker’s all-round contribution to his side’s performance. “I think he had a brilliant performance today,” Arteta said. “I think he scored an unbelievable goal, he has the quality to do that. “What I loved the most was how connected he was to the team. We used him many times in different ways, his link-up play, the way he holds the ball, the way he threads it in behind and stretches the pitch. “There was a lot to like in that performance and that’s everything that we need.” Arteta was also pleased with Arsenal’s overall display against Dortmund but felt his side should have taken more from the chances they created. “A brilliant performance,” he said. “The way we played, bearing in mind the opposition that we played today, to do what we’ve done out there is something to be very, very pleased with. “There’s very little more you can demand from the team, but obviously the feeling is that we should have rewarded ourselves much more when you put that kind of performance in with the amount of chances.”

item.title: Why Eagles’ Vic Fangio is sure Jonathan Greenard’s ankle injury is behind him, even if he’s banged up
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Why Eagles’ Vic Fangio is sure Jonathan Greenard’s ankle injury is behind him, even if he’s banged up appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Through the first eight weeks of the 2026 NFL season, the Philadelphia Eagles ’ decision to trade and extend Jonathan Greenard looked like a Bryce Huff-level mistake by Howie Roseman . Coming off a down season due to injuries, Greenard suffered an injury over the summer that caused him to miss the first two weeks of the season. When he did return, Greenard looked more like his 2025 self than his double-digit sack seasons from 2023-24, recording just two tackles, zero tackles for a loss, and zero sacks. However, over the past two weeks – with a bye in between them – Greenard appears to finally be back to 100 percent, recording four tackles, two tackles for a loss, and two sacks a game during the team’s recent defensive resurgence. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Discussing Greenard’s recent resurgence over the past few weeks, Vic Fangio joked that it sure looks like Greenard is back to 100 percent, even if he’s still working back to 100 percent with continued treatment. “Hopefully. I told him, I said [ jokingly. ], he’s had a sack in each of the last two games, and that sack dance or celebration that he does afterwards indicates to me that there’s nothing wrong with his ankle, so he shouldn’t even be getting any treatment anymore. But that is not the case. He’s not 100% yet.” Fangio also commented on the Eagles’ resurgent pass rush, which has amassed more sacks in the last two weeks (11) than in their first eight games of the season (10). While some may point to Greenard’s health or the emerging narrative that Jordan Davis was holding the pass rush back as a run-stuffing 2-tech, Fangio admitted he doesn’t really know, but he’s happy the production has finally matched the effort level. “I don’t know. Other than — I’ve been telling you guys that it would come, but you didn’t believe me,” Fangio said. “But the guy we’re playing this week, I think, is the hardest guy in the league to sack. I think they have the best sack percentage for an offense of not getting sacked.” Could the Eagles’ pass-rushing issues really come down to getting their best players healthy? Will a healthy Greenard, plus an ascending Nolan Smith, and a more pass-rushing-centric nose tackle like Byron Young suddenly allow the Eagles to average five sacks per game down the stretch? Only time will tell, but as Fangio noted, their next challenge against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving will be incredibly telling either way. item.title: Alexandersson a contender for Swansea job
item.description: Freyr Alexandersson has only been in charge at current club Rosenborg since June [Getty Images] Freyr Alexandersson has emerged as a contender to take charge at Swansea City following the shock exit of Vitor Matos. Interim boss Ashley Williams led Swansea for the second time as they were beaten 2-1 at Middlesbrough on Tuesday. But the club have spoken to a number of candidates over the head coach vacancy and Rosenborg boss Alexandersson is thought to be a frontrunner. After falling to a fifth defeat in seven matches despite a battling performance at Boro, Swansea now turn their attention to Sunday's south Wales derby against Cardiff City. As it stands, there is no certainty over whether a new coaching team will be in place for the Cardiff game. When asked whether clarity is needed as Swansea prepare to face their rivals, Williams said: "That's not for me to comment on. "My job was to get the boys ready for this game [at Middlesbrough] and I did the best I could do. Now my job will be to debrief this game and take it from there. "I know you want an answer but I can't give it to you because I have got work to do about this game first and foremost. We'll look at the weekend when the time comes I think." Icelander Alexandersson, 44, has only been in charge of Rosenborg since June. The Norwegian top-flight club were in relegation danger when he was appointed, but lie fourth with just three games remaining in the season, which concludes in mid-December. Alexandersson previously worked for another Norwegian side, Brann, but was sacked earlier this year after 15 months in charge. Prior to that, he was manager of Belgian side Kortrijk, who are a sister club of Cardiff. "It's no secret when I spoke to Kortrijk I also had a conversation with the management of Cardiff that I'm going to train in England, to be a manager in the Championship or Premier League," Alexandersson said at the time. item.title: Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund: The tactics board - How Niko Kovac's 53-clearance wall broke Mikel Arteta's 30-shot siege
item.description: Arsenal FC v Borussia Dortmund - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 - Getty Images Sport Arsenal dropped points at home in the Champions League league phase for the first time since the format was introduced, as Borussia Dortmund came from behind to draw 1-1 at the Emirates Stadium. On paper, the hosts were dominant. They had 63% of the ball, took 30 shots worth 2.34 expected goals (xG) and had 56 touches inside the Dortmund box. Yet both sides created four big chances, both had four shots on target, and Dortmund were the better team for long spells after the break. Viktor Gyokeres' long-range opener rewarded Arsenal's fast start, but Maximilian Beier's equaliser, made by a surging run from centre-back Joane Gadou, showed exactly where Arsenal were vulnerable. Arsenal's tactical setup Mikel Arteta lined up in a 4-2-3-1, with Declan Rice and Myles Lewis-Skelly in midfield behind Noni Madueke, Martin Odegaard and Christos Tzolis, and Gyokeres leading the line. Arsenal flew out of the blocks. Their press gave Dortmund no time on the ball in the opening 15 minutes, they completed 91% of their passes in the first half, and the opener arrived in the 10th minute when Madueke laid the ball into the path of Gyokeres, who sent a dipping 25-yard strike past Gregor Kobel. The right flank was Arsenal's main source of creativity. Madueke repeatedly got the better of Daniel Svensson , and he and Odegaard became the first Arsenal pair on record to create four or more chances each in a Champions League first half. On the other side, Piero Hincapie pushed high from left-back, joining attacks and even arriving at the back post for a header that Kobel saved early in the second half. The problem was the quality of Arsenal's chances. Eight of their 14 first-half shots came from outside the box, and the goal itself was worth just 0.03 xG. Set pieces made up 0.56 of their 0.94 first-half xG, and Madueke failed to bring down a rebound with the goal at his mercy in the 15th minute. Rice was the most dangerous runner from midfield, curling just over from distance in the 33rd minute and being denied by Nico Schlotterbeck's recovery tackle when through on goal two minutes later. Borussia Dortmund's tactical setup Niko Kovac set up with a back three of Gadou, Waldemar Anton and Schlotterbeck, with Julian Ryerson and Svensson as wing-backs, Felix Nmecha and Joey Veerman in central midfield, and Jobe Bellingham and Beier supporting Fabio Silva in attack. After a difficult opening quarter of an hour, Dortmund settled, won more of the midfield duels and began to look dangerous from set pieces, where Kepa Arrizabalaga, deputising for the injured David Raya, struggled to deal with high balls. Dortmund's main route forward was down the right. Half of their attacks came down that side, through Ryerson and Gadou, attacking the space Hincapie left behind when he pushed on. item.title: Arteta backs 'brilliant' Gyokeres after Arsenal waste chances to beat Dortmund
item.description: Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres in action against Borussia Dortmund (Ben Stansall) Mikel Arteta defended Viktor Gyokeres after the inconsistent Arsenal striker's "unbelievable" strike was followed by a costly miss in Tuesday's 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League. Arteta had urged Gyokeres to seize his opportunity after selecting the Sweden striker instead of Kai Havertz for the league phase tie at the Emirates Stadium. Initially, Gyokeres looked like doing just that with his first goal at home this season, and only his third for the Gunners in all competitions. But the 28-year-old has been much-maligned for his erratic displays since arriving from Sporting Lisbon in 2025. And he gave more ammunition to his critics when he missed a golden opportunity to seal the points with a woeful header in the closing stages. Leaping to Gyokeres's defence, Arteta said: "He had a brilliant performance today. He scored an unbelievable goal. He has the quality to do that. "What I loved the most was how connected he was to the team. We used him many times in different ways, his link-up play, the way he held the ball. "He got behind and stretched the pitch. There was a lot to like in that performance." Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 11 games in all competitions, but this was not a vintage display by the English champions, who failed to win at home for the first time this season. Arteta disagreed, insisting Arsenal were deserving of all three points on the balance of play. "The way we played, there is no question how superior, how dominant, how much of a threat we were. It was great to watch. It was unbelievable that sometimes the ball didn't go in the back of the net," he said. "The execution can be better, we rushed a little bit. Certainly we could have finished the actions better today. "There is an element of luck, how the hell some of those balls didn't go in, I don't know. There is an element of us needing to finish the actions better." - 'Courageous' - Arsenal sit fifth in the league phase with three wins and two draws from their five matches, while seventh-placed Dortmund are one point behind them. Arteta will hope for a much more ruthless display in a significant Premier League showdown with spluttering title rivals Manchester City in north London on Sunday. "What the team has shown today is a step in the right direction. There is a lot to like but obviously we want to win every game," he said. Dortmund had equalised through Maximilian Beier prior to Gyokeres's key miss. The Bundesliga leaders were well worth a point for their gritty display and boss Niko Kovac said: "This is a big one for all of us, the players, the fans and the club -- a big point away to Arsenal. "In the first 15 minutes we didn't play the way I hoped. We were too passive. "We were more courageous and pressed more actively after the break. We got Arsenal into difficult situations. "We came back because of our huge desire. I'm really happy for the boys." smg/bsp

item.title: We have to stay positive, urges Haaland
item.description: We have to stay positive, urges Haaland Erling Haaland has called for everyone associated with City to remain upbeat following our 2-2 UEFA Champions League draw with Napoli on Tuesday night. Match Report City hit back twice to share the spoils with Napoli Rasmus Højlund opened the scoring for the visitors at the Etihad Stadium after 55 minutes, before Ayyoub Bouaddi smashed in his first goal for City to level. Noa Lang struck the Italian side back ahead before Rayan Cherki drilled us level with four minutes left to play. The draw means Enzo Maresca’s side have one win in our last five matches across all competitions but Haaland, who captained City on the night, has believes a positive mindset will prove to be the best way to bring out the quality of everyone in the squad. “Football is so easy and so difficult,” he said after the draw. “When you win games everything is easy and you know what to do, and when you don’t win you start to question everything. The perfect thing to do is don’t think. “We have so much quality so it’s about getting that quality out of every single player. “We have to regroup, stay positive, bring all the energy on the pitch and try to do the best we can. “We missed a goal. item.title: Rasmus Hojlund marks goal against Manchester City with provocative celebration
item.description: Rasmus Hojlund celebrated his opening goal in Napoli ’s 2-2 draw with Manchester City with a provocative gesture towards the home fans, telling them, “There’s only one club in Manchester”. The Dane drilled a fine low finish past City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma in the 55th minute of Tuesday night’s Champions League group stage encounter. But City twice came from behind to rescue a point , with Ayyoub Bouaddi and Rayan Cherki scoring for the home side either side of Noa Lang’s crisp volley. After breaking the deadlock Hojlund celebrated in front of the home fans, holding up one finger and saying, “There’s only one club in Manchester”, having spent two seasons at Manchester United before joining Napoli. He explained the celebration in an interview on TNT Sports afterwards: “Some good banter, there’s the rivalry between Manchester City and Man United and I obviously have a past in Manchester United, so that’s my club - nothing against Man City, but United is my club.” Asked whether it meant more to score at the Etihad , he said: “Yeah, good to score here, a good point, so happy for that.” Hojlund swapped Atalanta for Old Trafford in a £72m move in 2023, but was loaned to Napoli after two seasons, having underwhelmed in a particularly difficult second year at the club in which he endured a 21-game goalless run. He scored 26 goals in 95 appearances. The 23-year-old then completed a £38m move to the Serie A side this summer, with Napoli obliged to buy him permanently after qualifying for the Champions League. Napoli appeared much the happier side after their draw with City despite twice surrendering the lead, with the hosts having won only once in their past seven games in all competitions. Hojlund added: “I wouldn’t say it was a free game but it’s one of those were you go, OK, let’s see if we can get something. And actually I’m a bit gutted because we could probably have got all three points today.”

Now, the SEC is preparing to consider a response that would have seemed almost unthinkable just a few months ago. item.description: Best defender in the World? Upamecano sends confident message ahead of UCL clash against Lille Dayot Upamecano is looking forward to a special Champions League encounter when Bayern Munich take on Lille on Wednesday. The French defender has fond memories of the region, having spent part of his youth at Valenciennes. "It's a very special game for me. I was in Valenciennes, and Lille was like the north derby for me. I'm very happy to play here," Upamecano said at Tuesday's press conference. The 28-year-old has also earned plenty of recognition for his performances this season, with some going as far as calling him the best defender in the world . However, Upamecano was quick to remain modest when asked about the label. "Well, best defender in the world? That's an honour, but it's also kind of a big statement. I'm trying my very best. I work with my teammates and also with the coach. I just want to win every game that we play, and I'm fully focused on tomorrow's game." The defender also spoke about Jamal Musiala, who is working his way back to full fitness. Upamecano is delighted to have the attacking midfielder as a teammate rather than an opponent. "Jamal is there. He's very, very difficult to play against. In training, he always gives 100%. I'm glad to be playing alongside him. It's much, much better than having him as an opponent." Bayern are dealing with several injury problems ahead of the trip to Lille, but Upamecano is confident that the squad has enough quality to cope with the absences. “It's quite a challenging period. item.title: Copa America Confirmed for Return to the United States in 2028
item.description: CONMEBOL and CONCACAF made a joint announcement today, confirming what had long been rumored, that the Copa America will return to the United States in 2028. It will be the third edition played in the United States, after the 2016 Centenario and 2024, and the second in a row hosted outside South America. In 2024, Argentina defeated Colombia in Miami to retain their title, while previously, Chile had won the 2016 edition played in the United States by defeating Argentina. Copa America Confirmed for June 2028 The 2028 edition will be played at stadiums across the United States from June 9th to July 9th, and 16 teams will be entrants. That’s the 10 teams from South America that are CONMEBOL members, and 6 more from CONCACAF. The CONCACAF entrants will be confirmed based on how teams perform in the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup , which is also hosted in the United States next summer. The final on July 9th lands just days before the Los Angeles Olympics open, in the one clean window of a crowded American summer. Why the United States again? Here is the answer nobody bothers to hide. More than 1.5 million fans attended the 2024 edition, and the money in the American market is money no South American host can match. The tournament has become a cash machine, and no bid from South America can compete with it. That is simply the reality of where the sport’s economy now sits. “The CONMEBOL Copa América is much more than a tournament: it is part of our identity, our history and the greatness of South American football,” CONMEBOL president Alejandro Domínguez said. “In 2028, we will once again bring that passion to the United States, reaffirming our historic partnership with CONCACAF.” The tournament was first played in 1916 and lived its entire life in South America. It will now have been staged in the United States three times in twelve years. The case is not only financial. The venues are modern, safe and high quality, the organization of events is reliable, despite the security issues at the stadium in Miami for the 2024 final, and the United States based diaspora fills stadiums for teams that would play in front of empty seats elsewhere. Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru, and Mexico all draw like home teams in American stadiums, because for millions of their fans, it is home. Concacaf president Victor Montagliani pointed to the sporting side of the deal. “After our collaboration in 2024, we are pleased to join forces again to bring the CONMEBOL Copa America to our region in 2028,” he said, adding that the agreement will give six Concacaf national teams a new opportunity to compete against some of the best in the world. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.title: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟
item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. He has since collected four senior caps and added another milestone to his résumé by scoring against Mexico at 17 years and five days old, making him the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
